statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. CME equity-index futures have been halted since the Friday 21:00 UTC settle, so no Nasdaq-100 price path exists in the current hour and Tail stays on the closed-venue floor of 5%. Stress eases one point to 55%: the IRGC claim published at roughly 03:03 UTC that its naval force struck a US unmanned surface vessel in the Strait of Hormuz has now stood for an hour without CENTCOM confirmation or denial and without a follow-on step, and the target was unmanned, which keeps the sequence below the casualty threshold that would justify a wider allowance. The scheduled 22:00 UTC reopen and the first full hour after it remain the two WATCH slots of this horizon.
recommendation: Tail holds the 5% closed-venue floor through the dormant weekend hours, lifts from the tenth slot as a conditional pre-auction gap allowance and peaks at 14% in the final full hour of the halt, so the deterministic mapping stays EA_ON and green for the first eighteen published hours. The 22:00 UTC reopening hour and the first full hour after it are each scored at 20% Tail and therefore map to WATCH and yellow; together they form the only published danger window. The last four slots step back to 17%, 15%, 14% and 13% and to green on the assumption of an orderly two-way auction into the shortened US Labor Day futures session. Stress runs from 55% down to a 53% low in the quiet Sunday hours, rebuilds to a 71% peak at the reopen and enters the high band from the sixteenth slot onward. Confidence declines from 85% to 72% as later slots rest on progressively older Friday-dated evidence.
headline: Nasdaq-100 unquoted at 29,544.16 with about eighteen hours of the CME weekend halt left; the IRGC claim of a strike on a US unmanned surface vessel in Hormuz has stood unconfirmed for an hour, easing Stress to 55% while Tail remains on the closed-venue floor
body:
The Nasdaq-100 closed the August payroll session on Friday 4 September at 29,544.16, up about 62 points or 0.21% from a 29,482.30 previous close, after ranging between 29,440.15 and 29,655.22. Price retraced repeatedly in both directions inside that 215-point range, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure that the Tail score measures. CME equity-index futures have been halted since the Friday 21:00 UTC settle and are scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on 6 September. That reopening hour and the first full hour after it are the two WATCH slots of this forecast.

The geopolitical sequence produced no new verified step during the current hour. The most recent development remains the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps statement carried at about 03:03 UTC, saying its naval force struck an American unmanned surface vessel attempting to enter what it described as a restricted area of the Strait of Hormuz, together with a demand that the United States leave the region. That claim has now stood for an hour with no CENTCOM confirmation or denial and no corroborating report. It follows Saturday's exchange, in which US Central Command said it had disabled two Iranian crude tankers and destroyed a third after Iranian ballistic missiles were fired toward a US aircraft carrier and a destroyer, with no US personnel injured and neither vessel hit, and the IRGC counter-claim of attacks on three tankers and three US-affiliated ships. An unresolved military exchange at a shipping chokepoint with a closed equity venue raises Stress rather than Tail, because Tail measures an observable pathological price path and no price path can exist while the venue is shut. The absence of a further step over the past hour is the reason Stress eases by one point rather than extending its rise.

The macro impulse into the halt is hawkish. August non-farm payrolls printed 162,000 against roughly 53,000 expected, and the unemployment rate held at 4.1%. The Federal Reserve H.15 release dated 4 September carries a 2-year constant maturity yield of 4.34% and a 10-year of 4.77% for the preceding business day, with reporting around the print describing the 2-year as reaching its highest level since January 2025. WTI trades around 91.48 dollars after a weekly gain of more than 9%, its strongest week since mid-July, on Hormuz supply risk, with Brent near 95 dollars. Against that, the VIX closed at 14.53 inside a 13.80 to 14.58 range, an unusually calm volatility anchor for a week carrying an active naval conflict.

Cross-asset tone into the halt was rotational rather than one-way: semiconductors led while application and infrastructure software fell, and the Nasdaq-100 rose while broader large-cap and industrial benchmarks did not. Dispersion of that kind reduces directional conviction and argues against the aligned-breadth condition that would amplify Tail. The shared Finviz cross-asset context file was collected at 01:22 UTC and is therefore about three hours old at this assessment time, well beyond the ninety-minute freshness threshold; it was read as stale supporting context only, is latest-session rather than live, and was not used as evidence of any current Nasdaq-100 structure.

The forward risk concentrates in one place. Roughly eighteen hours of unpriced information, an unresolved military exchange at a shipping chokepoint, an energy premium and untested hawkish rate pricing all meet a single opening auction rather than a continuous session. Monday 7 September is the US Labor Day holiday, so cash equities and the bond market are closed and the futures session that follows the reopen is shortened and thinner. That concentration is scored as a 20% Tail allowance in the 22:00 and 23:00 UTC slots, which maps to WATCH and yellow and forms the only published danger window, then steps down to 17%, 15%, 14% and 13%. It is a conditional gap-and-extension allowance, not an assertion that directional structure has been observed; if the reopening auction instead shows shallow pullbacks and repeated extension after failed retracements, later assessments will revise those slots upward on observed evidence.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours run from 04:00 UTC on 5 September to 03:00 UTC on 6 September and lie entirely inside the CME weekend halt. All 24 slots are available from published Claude assessments, every one is scored at the closed-venue Tail floor of 4-5% under a normal mode, and every one maps to EA_ON and green. Stress was flat at 38% from 04:00 UTC through 10:00 UTC, climbed from 39% at 11:00 UTC to 42% by 14:00 UTC as the Saturday US-Iran sequence developed, stepped to 48% at 15:00 UTC once the CENTCOM tanker strikes were verified, rose to 52% by 19:00 UTC and peaked at 57% at 20:00 UTC when the IRGC counter-claim and Iran's threat of more severe attacks were published. It then eased to 53% by 02:00 UTC as the sequence went quiet, before the closing slot lifted it to 56% on the newly published IRGC unmanned-vessel claim. Confidence held in a narrow 85-86% band throughout: the assessment kept current verified levels, yields, oil, volatility and calendar coverage, but no live Nasdaq-100 price path existed in any of the 24 hours.
outlookSummary: Eighteen of the twenty-four published hours fall inside the CME weekend halt, so no observable Nasdaq-100 price path can form in them; the mapped policy state stays EA_ON with Tail on the 5% closed-venue floor through the dormant hours, lifting from 13:00 UTC as a conditional pre-auction gap allowance and peaking at 14% in the last full hour of the halt. The final six slots are different: futures are scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on 6 September, so those hours are the first in which structure can exist. The reopening hour and the first full hour after it each carry a 20% Tail allowance, map to WATCH and yellow, and together form the only published danger window; the last four slots step back to 17%, 15%, 14% and 13% and to green on the assumption of an orderly auction into the shortened US Labor Day futures session. Stress opens at 55%, reaches a 53% low in the quiet Sunday hours, then rebuilds through the afternoon to a 71% peak at the reopen before easing to 62%. Confidence declines from 85% to 72% because every later slot rests on Friday-dated market evidence and on a geopolitical sequence whose latest step is still an unconfirmed IRGC claim.
